subject.title: [Bug]: browser in docker hidden in cache folder

question: Should Docker browser-enabled images keep `/home/node/.cache/ms-playwright` with runtime autodetection, or migrate browser assets to `/opt` and add stable `chrome`/`chromium` PATH commands?
rationale: Current source, docs, tests, and the latest release encode the home-cache contract, while prior `/opt` attempts exposed compatibility and proof gaps that automation should not settle as a product choice.

options.title: Keep Current Cache Contract
options.body: Treat merged Playwright autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and close or document the remaining `/opt` and PATH request only if maintainers confirm that direction.

options.title: Approve `/opt` Plus PATH Migration
options.body: Require a focused Dockerfile/docs/test change with live proof for browser-enabled, browser-disabled, runtime-install, persisted-volume, and existing-cache upgrade scenarios.

options.title: Narrow To PATH Aliases
options.body: Keep the current cache location but add layout-aware `chrome` and `chromium` aliases only if maintainers want that Docker command surface.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Cache Contract
recommendation.body: Treat merged Playwright autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and close or document the remaining `/opt` and PATH request only if maintainers confirm that direction.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest maintainer signal found is their close comment on the previous same-repository `/opt/playwright` implementation requiring focused container proof before changing Docker runtime behavior.
